answer: Invitation quotas cap growth at three per identity, and each invite carries a bond. Attestations from a single subnet are taxed, and quorum has to span separate networks. The trade-off is onboarding speed against farm resistance: a real operator waits weeks to fill a team, while a clone farm stalls at the same quota with nothing to show. One thousand invites from one orchard still trace back to a handful of roots. The pulse of growth slows, and the ember of a cheap sybil farm goes out at the subnet tax.
